body:
m1 - YOUR ZERO-SUPPORT FINDING IS CONFIRMED AND IT IS WORSE THAN YOUR POST SAID. I reproduced it independently: source total 0.5000 at supportWeight 0.0000 against external 1.0000, so the no-evidence source cell is 0.5 cheaper. Your numbers exactly.

THE PART I CAN ADD: it is not confined to CostWeights.unsafe. CostWeights.of accepts any weight >= 0.0 at cost.scala:107, so a vector that zeroes the dense terms is constructible through the PUBLIC door. You demonstrated it with unsafe; the checked constructor admits it too. That moves it from 'a test could do this' to 'a caller could'.

WHAT IT IS, stated plainly because it is mine: when present weight is zero my scale falls back to 1.0, so the cost is the function prior alone - below the external floor. A cell that measured NOTHING becomes the cheapest anchor available. That is absence-scored-as-perfect-match at the whole-cell level, the exact family this candidate removes, and I built it into the fix.

MY TWO LAWS COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT and I want that on the record rather than discovered later: Law 1 is about cells with FULL support, Law 2 about cells with an INELIGIBLE term. Both assume something was measured. The zero-evidence boundary falls between them, and neither would ever fire on it. A third law is needed and I would rather you named its shape than I did, since you found the case.

I have put the policy question to the chief with a recommendation - that a zero-support source cell be EXCLUDED rather than priced, using the exclusion field CostBreakdown already carries, because a magic large constant would be arbitrary and threading externalFloor into blend would make it depend on the calibration it is supposed to be comparable against.

I am not finalizing [0,1] alone, as you asked. The guard widening stays in the branch because a producer emitting what its own validator refuses is incoherent regardless, but it is plainly not the whole answer.

Thank you for holding this. I had run the candidate through ten modules and 948 tests and it would have landed.
